newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. sign hydropower cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. sign hydropower cooperation pact.

text.p: Water authorities from China and the United States have signed a memorandum of understanding to develop China's water resources and exchange hydropower technology, the China Daily said on Thursday.

The pact, signed on Tuesday by officials from China's Ministry of Water Resources and the Tennessee Valley Authority of the United States, would boost cooperation in developing power projects on the Hanjiang River in China's central provinces of Shaanxi and Hubei, the newspaper said.
The Hanjiang is the largest tributary of the Yangtze River, where China is working on the colossal Three Gorges Dam project.
Beijing plans to build 12 hydroelectric plants on the Hanjiang that would generate 13.8 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity a year, it said.

"China has the greatest hydropower potential in the world but only less than 14 percent of the total resources has been exploited," the newspaper quoted Minister of Water Resources Niu Maosheng as saying.
The Tennessee Valley Authority would also help upgrade existing power plants and provide technical training to Chinese staff, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
